workbench.title: Workbench
workbench.intro: Five ways to test the list before you sign it off. Each one changes how you see the evidence, none of them changes it behind your back.

duel.name: Duel
duel.short: Pick the more important of two requirements, a few times in a row. We turn your choices into priority weights you can apply.
duel.help: Click the side that matters more. There is no wrong answer, we only learn what you value.

arena.name: Conflict arena
arena.short: Where customers disagree, both sides stand next to each other with their own quotes.
arena.help: We never average a conflict away. Read both sides, then decide on the requirement.

assumptions.name: Assumption switch
assumptions.short: Turn off the factors that are guesses about the future and see which requirements still hold up.
assumptions.help: Solid requirements keep their rank without assumptions. Those that drop rely on a bet about 2030.

voices.name: Customer voices
voices.short: Every quote behind the list, with its ID, so you can read what people actually wrote.
voices.help: Team picks are pinned at the top. Every card shows which requirement it supports.

swipe.name: Decision run
swipe.short: Go through open requirements one by one. Approve or reject, always with a reason.
swipe.help: Your reason is stored in the audit trail next to your name. Without a reason the buttons stay locked.
